interest: Shows 1932 U.S. assessment of Japan's economic endurance after the Manchurian Incident, amid Depression-era budget cuts to telegraphic reporting.
overview: Docket sheets for file 894.50 (1930-1932) list reports on Japan's Depression-era economy—trade, gold reserves, and Diet loans for Manchuria—including a detailed Neville telegram on cotton, silk, steel, cement, shipping, and bank conditions.

people.name: Toshihiko Taketomi
people.role: Chief of Bureau of Commercial Affairs

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Department of State List of Papers docket sheets indexing diplomatic and consular communications on Japanese economic, financial, and industrial conditions from 1930 to 1932.
subfiles.summary: Lists 1930-1932 docket entries for file 894.50 on Japan's economic depression, trade balances, and Manchurian military appropriations, including reports by Garrels, Forbes, and Neville on cotton, silk, steel, copper, cement, shipping, and banking.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Japan, Economic Matters (894.50, Sub-numbers 50-71)
